Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:10:1.english: What is the permission? - [That] of Rabba bar Ḥana.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:10:2.hebrew: יורה - איסור והיתר. אמר להם רבי: יורה. ולקמן פריך: אי גמיר, למה ליה רשותא בהוראה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:10:2.english: May he instruct - [Regarding matters of] the forbidden and the permitted. Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] said to them: "He may instruct." And later on, [the Gemara] asks: If he is learned, why does he need authorization to instruct?

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:10:3.english: May he adjudicate - With authorization, and be exempt from paying [if he errs].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:10:4.hebrew: יתיר בבכורות - יראה במומין, ואם קבוע הוא, יתירנו לשוחטו; דביומיה דרבי אין לבכור תקנה עד שיפול בו מום, דאחר חורבן היה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:10:4.english: May he permit firstborn [animals] - He may inspect blemishes, and if it is permanent, he may permit it to be slaughtered; for in the days of Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], a firstborn has no remedy until a blemish falls upon it, as [his era] was after the Destruction [of the Temple].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:11:1.english: He may not declare [firstborn animals] permitted - [The Gemara] explains the reason below.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:12:1.hebrew: איבו - אבוה דרב הוה, כדאמרינן באור לארבעה עשר (פסחים דף ד.): א"ל אייבו קיים כו':
Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:12:1.english: Aivu - He was the father of Rav, as we say in [the chapter entitled] Or Le’arba’ah Asar (Pesachim 4a): He said to him: “Is Aivu alive?,” etc.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:12:2.english: And Ḥana - [He was] the father of Rabba [bar Ḥana].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:12:3.english: From Kafrei - [The name of a] place.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:1:1.hebrew: דן אפילו ביחיד - דכתיב (ויקרא יט) בצדק תשפוט, וקסבר: אין כאן עירוב פרשיות:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:1:1.english: He may judge even as a lone [judge] - For it is written (Leviticus 19:15): “In righteousness shall you judge [your neighbor],” and he holds [that] there is no merging of [Torah] portions here.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:2:1.english: That I have learned - Traditions of laws from my teachers.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:2:2.english: And [can] extrapolate - I know how to add and explain reasons from my own understanding.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:2:3.hebrew: ונקיטנא רשותא - מריש גלותא, דייננא דיני ממונות ביחידי:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:2:3.english: And I have received permission - From the Exilarch, [and therefore] I judge cases of monetary law as a lone judge.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:2:4.english: His judgment is not a judgment - And the judgment is completely reversed:

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:3:1.english: Adjudicated a case - As a lone [judge].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:3:2.hebrew: אי קבלוך עלייהו - לגמרי, לילך אחריך אם לדין אם לטעות, ולא יתבעוך — לא תשלם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:3:2.english: If they accepted you upon themselves - Completely, to follow you, whether for [correct] judgment or for error, and that they would not claim against you — you do not pay.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:3:3.hebrew: ואי לא זיל שלים - ואי לא קבלו טעותך עליהם, דאמרו לך: "דיינת לן דין תורה" — זיל שלים. ומיהו מיהדר דינא לא, אלמא גמיר וסביר, וכי לא נקיט רשותא דיניה דינא, ולא מהדר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:3:3.english: And if not, go pay - And if they did not accept your error upon themselves, as they said to you: "You judged us [according to] Torah law" — go pay. But nevertheless, reversing the judgment is not [done]; evidently, [he is] learned and has reasoned understanding, and when one did not receive permission, his judgment is [a valid] judgment, and is not reversed.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:4:1.hebrew: לישקול רשותא - דכיון דברשות נחת, לא משלם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:4:1.english: Let him take permission - For since he entered [upon judging] with permission, he does not pay.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:5:1.english: From here to here - From the Exilarch to Babylonia, to judge cases in Babylonia.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:5:2.english: And from there to there - From the Nasi of Eretz Yisrael to judge in Eretz Yisrael.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:5:3.hebrew: שבט - לשון שררה, ויש להן רשות להפקיר, דהפקר ב"ד הפקר, דכתיב (עזרא י): "וכל אשר לא יבא" וגו', ביבמות בהאשה רבה (יבמות דף פט:):
Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:5:3.english: A scepter - An expression of authority, and they have the authority to declare [property] ownerless, for property declared ownerless by a court is ownerless, as it is written (Ezra 10:8): “And whoever does not come...” etc., [as expounded] in Yevamot, in [the chapter entitled] HaIsha Rabbah (Yevamot 89b).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:6:1.english: Who subjugate the people - For they have the power and authority from the kings of Persia.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:6:2.hebrew: בני בניו של הלל - הלל נשיא היה, כדאמר בפסחים באלו דברים (פסחים דף סו.): הושיבוהו בראש ומינוהו נשיא עליהם:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:6:2.english: The grandchildren of Hillel - Hillel was the Nasi, as [the Gemara] says in Pesachim in [the chapter entitled] Elu Devarim (Pesachim 66a): “They seated him at the head and appointed him Nasi over them.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:7:1.english: Adjudicated a case - In Babylonia, and erred.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:7:2.hebrew: אתא - לא"י, לקמיה דרבי חייא:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:7:2.english: He came - To Eretz Yisrael, before Rabbi Ḥiyya.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:7:3.hebrew: ש"מ מהתם להכא לא מהני - דהא רבה בר חנה רשותא הוה נקיט מרבי, דנשיא דא"י היה, כדאמרן לקמן בשמעתין: בן אחי יורד לבבל וכו':
Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:7:3.english: Learn from it [that permission] from there to here is not effective - For Rabba bar Ḥana had received authorization from Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who was the Nasi of Eretz Yisrael, as we say later in our sugya: "My brother's son is going down to Babylonia, etc."

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:8:1.english: Not from you did I receive permission - And I am not subordinate to you.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 5a:9:1.english: On the borders - Which are drawn after Eretz Yisrael.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:1:1.hebrew: ואם היה מומחה לרבים כו' - פירש הקונטרס: דכתיב "בצדק תשפוט", וקסבר אין עירוב פרשיות כתיב כאן. וקשה: דא"כ, תקשה ליה הך ברייתא לר' אבהו, דאמר: "שנים שדנו — אין דיניהם דין", לד"ה! וע"ק: דמשמע לפי' הקונטרס דלמאן דאית ליה עירוב פרשיות אין יכול לדון יחידי, והא רב יוסף ס"ל בפ' המגרש (גיטין דף פח:) דבהודאות והלואות עבדינן שליחותייהו, אלמא אית ליה עירוב פרשיות, ואפ"ה משמע בסמוך מעובדא דמר זוטרא דאית ליה לרב יוסף דיחיד מומחה דן, ואפי' יחידי! ועוד, מדקאמר בסמוך: "אבל לא נקיט רשותא — דיניה לאו דינא", משמע דסבר כר' אבהו, ואפי' הכי יחיד מומחה דן — דלשמואל אפילו יחיד שאינו מומחה דינו דין, דלאו דוקא נקט שמואל "שנים", כמו שאפרש לקמן בע"ה; ודוחק לפרש "דיניה לאו דינא" — לכתחלה. לכך נ"ל: דאפי' למאן דבעי ג' מומחין מדאורייתא, תקנתא דרבנן היא דיחיד מומחה לרבים דן אפי' יחידי. והשתא, הא דקאמר "דיניה לאו דינא", לאו אכגון דרב נחמן קאי — דאיהו סבר לה כשמואל לקמן דשנים שדנו דיניהן דין — אלא אכגון אנא דר' חייא קאי, דלית ליה דשמואל. ולהאי פי', הא דפריך לקמן (סנהדרין דף ו.) לר' אבהו מדן את הדין, ה"מ לשנויי דמיירי ביחיד מומחה לרבים. ומיהו קשה: דבפרק ראוהו בית דין (ר"ה דף כה:) משמע דמדאורייתא קאמר דמומחה לרבים דן ביחידי, דתנן התם: "שאין היחיד נאמן ע"פ עצמו", ומפרש בגמרא דאיצטריך למיתני דלא תימא דנאמן, מידי דהוה איחיד מומחה דהכא, ופריך: "ואימא ה"נ?", ומשני: "אין לך מומחה יותר ממשה" — ואי מדרבנן, מאי מייתי ממשה? וי"ל: דהתם פריך ומשני למ"ד לעיל דבר תורה חד נמי כשר:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:1:1.english: "And if he was an expert for the public, etc." - Rashi explained that it is written: "In righteousness shall you judge [your neighbor]" (Leviticus 19:15), and he maintains that there is no juxtaposition of passages written here. And this is difficult: for if so, this baraita should present a difficulty to Rabbi Abbahu, who said: "If two judged, their judgment is not a [valid] judgment," according to all opinions! And furthermore, it is difficult: for according to Rashi's explanation, it implies that according to the one who maintains that there is a juxtaposition of passages, one cannot judge alone; yet Rav Yosef maintains in the chapter [entitled] HaMegoresh (Gittin 88b) that in [cases of] admissions and loans we act as their agents, which proves that he maintains [that there is] a juxtaposition of passages, and even so, it is implied nearby from the incident involving Mar Zutra that Rav Yosef maintains that a single expert may judge, and even alone! And furthermore, since [the Gemara] states nearby: "But if he did not obtain permission, his judgment is not a judgment," this implies that it holds in accordance with Rabbi Abbahu, and even so, a single expert may judge — for according to Shmuel, even a single [judge] who is not an expert, his judgment is a [valid] judgment, as Shmuel did not mention "two" strictly, as I will explain below, with the help of Heaven; and it is forced to explain "his judgment is not a judgment" [as meaning merely] ab initio. Therefore, it seems to me: even according to the one who requires three experts by biblical law, it is a rabbinic enactment that an expert for the public may judge even alone. And now, that which [the Gemara] says: "his judgment is not a judgment," does not refer to [a case] such as that of Rav Naḥman — for he holds in accordance with Shmuel below that if two judged, their judgment is a [valid] judgment — but rather refers to [a case] such as "I" of Rabbi Ḥiyya, who does not hold in accordance with Shmuel. And according to this explanation, that which [the Gemara] challenges Rabbi Abbahu below (Sanhedrin 6a) from [the mishnah stating]: "[If one] judged the case...", it could have answered that it is dealing with a single expert for the public. However, this is difficult: for in the chapter [entitled] Ra'uhu Beit Din (Rosh Hashanah 25b), it implies that it states that an expert for the public may judge alone by biblical law; as we learned in a mishnah there: "A single person is not believed on his own authority," and the Gemara explains that it was necessary to teach [this] so that you should not say that he is believed, just as is the case with a single expert here; and [the Gemara] challenges: "And let us say that indeed [he is believed]!", and answers: "You have no greater expert than Moses" — but if [judging alone] is [only] by rabbinic enactment, why does it cite [a proof] from Moses? And one can answer that there [in Rosh Hashanah], it asks and answers according to the one who said above that by biblical law, one [judge] is also qualified.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:1:2.hebrew: מומחה לרבים כו' - אע"ג דהאי מומחה לרבים היינו גמירנא וסבירנא, כדמסיק — מ"מ הא דקאמר לקמן בזה בורר (סנהדרין דף כג.): "לעולם פוסל והולך עד שיקבל עליו בפני ב"ד שמומחה לרבים", לאו דניבעי גמיר וסביר כר' חייא ורב נחמן; דהתם ב"ד קאמר, וכיון שהם ג', אפי' סתם בני אדם מומחין לרבים, אבל יחיד לא חשיב מומחה לרבים עד דגמיר וסביר:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:1:2.english: An expert for the public, etc. - Even though this "expert for the public" means [one who has] learned and reasoned, as [the Gemara] concludes later, nevertheless, that which it says later in [the chapter entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 23a): "He may continually disqualify [judges] until he accepts [to be judged] before a court that is an expert for the public" — [this] does not mean that we require [them to be] learned and reasoned like Rabbi Ḥiyya and Rav Naḥman; for there it says "a court," and since they are three, even ordinary people are [considered] experts for the public, but a lone [judge] is not considered an expert for the public until he is learned and reasoned.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:1:3.hebrew: דן אפי' יחידי - ויכול לכוף את האדם בעל כרחו; דאי בדקבליה עילויה — אפי' שאינו מומחה נמי. ומכאן, דסתם ג' יכולין לדון את האדם בעל כרחו, כשאינו רוצה לבא לב"ד, דהא ג' במקום יחיד מומחה קיימי. ואפי' שנים נמי דנין את האדם בעל כרחו, אלא דאיקרו "בית דין חצוף"; דאי בדקבלו עלייהו מיירי שמואל, אמאי הוי ב"ד חצוף? והא דתנן (לקמן סנהדרין דף כג.): "זה בורר לו אחד וזה בורר לו אחד", משמע דמדעתו — אין, בעל כרחו — לא? הני מילי כשאומר "לא אדון לפני זה אלא לפני זה", אבל אם אמר שלא יבא כלל לב"ד, או אם הוה לווה ואינו רוצה לדון כלל בעירו — כופין אותו ודנין אותו בעל כרחו:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:1:3.english: "He may judge even alone" - And he can coerce the person against his will; for if [it refers to a case] where he accepted him upon himself, even [a judge] who is not an expert [may] also [judge alone]. And from here [it is derived] that an ordinary [court of] three can judge a person against his will when he does not want to come to court, for three stand in the place of a single expert. And even two also judge a person against his will, but they are called an "insolent court"; for if Shmuel is dealing with [a case where] they accepted them upon themselves, why would they be an insolent court? And as for that which we learned [in the Mishnah] (below, Sanhedrin 23a): "This one chooses one [judge] and that one chooses one [judge]," which implies that with his consent, yes, [but] against his will, no — that applies only when he says, "I will not be judged before this [judge], but rather before this [other judge]"; but if he said that he will not come to court at all, or if he was a borrower and does not want to be judged in his city at all, they coerce him and judge him against his will.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:1:4.hebrew: כגון אנא דן דיני ממונות ביחידי - והא דתנן במסכת אבות (פ"ד מ"ח): "אל תהי דן יחידי, שאין דן יחידי אלא אחד" — הקב"ה — עצה טובה קמ"ל, שלא יטעה. והא דאמר "כגון אנא" כו' — היינו כלומר: יכול לדון, ולא שהיה דן; אי נמי: רגיל היה בדינין, ואין לחוש שמא יטעה:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:1:4.english: "One such as I may judge cases of monetary law as the lone judge" - And that which we learned in the Mishnah in tractate Avot (chapter 4, mishnah 8): "Do not judge alone, for none may judge alone except One" — namely the Holy One, blessed be He — the Mishnah comes to teach us good advice, so that one will not err. And that which he said, "One such as I" etc. — this means to say that he is permitted to judge, but not that he actually would judge; alternatively, he was well-versed in judgments, and there is no concern lest he err.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:3:1.hebrew: ואי לא זיל שלים - פירש בקונטרס: ואי לא, כגון דאמרי ליה: "דיינת לן דין תורה". וקשה: דאם כן, מאי דייק מהכא? דהא אפילו לא גמיר וסביר נמי, מה שעשה עשוי וישלם מביתו, כדמוכח לקמן (סנהדרין דף ו.), דפריך לרבי אבהו מדן את הדין, ומוקי לה בדקבלה עילויה, ובשאינו מומחה איירי, דהא קתני סיפא: ואם היה מומחה לרבים — פטור. לכך נראה: ואי לא — דלא קבלוך עלייהו כלל:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:3:1.english: "And if not, go and pay" - The kuntres explained: "And if not" — such as where they said to him: "Judge for us according to Torah law." And this is difficult: For if so, what does the Gemara infer from here? For even if he had neither learned nor possessed reasoning ability, what he did is done and he must pay from his own home, as is proven below (Sanhedrin 6a), where it raises an objection against Rabbi Abbahu from "if one judged the case," and establishes it as being where they accepted him upon themselves, and it is dealing with one who is not an expert, since the concluding clause teaches: "And if he was an expert to the public, he is exempt." Therefore it appears: "And if not" — that they did not accept you upon themselves at all.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:5:1.hebrew: דהכא שבט והתם מחוקק - משמע דשבט עדיף. והא דאמר בפרק מקום שנהגו (פסחים דף נא. ושם): "אבל מבבל לא"י, כיון דאנן כייפינן להו — עבדינן כוותייהו"? ואומר רבינו תם: דה"מ במילתא דאיסור והיתר, דבני א"י חכימי טפי, דאוירא דא"י מחכים, כדאמר הכא דאיקרו מחוקק שמלמדין תורה ברבים; אבל לענין הפקעת ממון ליפטר, דהפקר בית דין הפקר — עדיפי בני בבל, דאיקרו שבט, שרודין את העם במקל. והיינו טעמא: משום דראש גולה מזכרים, ונשיא שבא"י מנקבות, כדאמר בירושלמי:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:5:1.english: "Since here [they are] a scepter, and there [they are] a staff" - This implies that a scepter is superior. And as for that which [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Makom Shenahagu (Pesachim 51a and there): "However, from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael, since we are subordinate to them, we act in accordance with their [customs]"? And Rabbeinu Tam says that these words [apply] to matters of prohibition and permission, for the people of Eretz Yisrael are wiser, as the air of Eretz Yisrael makes [one] wise, as [the Gemara] says here that they are called "staff" because they teach Torah in public; but with regard to the expropriation of money to be exempt [from restitution if an authorized judge errs] — for the court's expropriation of property is valid expropriation — the people of Babylonia are superior, for they are called "scepter," since they subjugate the people with a rod. And this is the reason: because the Exilarch [descends] from males, and the Nasi in Eretz Yisrael [descends] from females, as [the Gemara] says in the Yerushalmi.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:7:1.hebrew: רבה בר חנה - גרסינן: דאי רבה בר בר חנה, א"כ היה בן בנו של חנה; והכא משמע דבן אחיו של ר' חייא היה, וחנה אחיו של ר' חייא היה, כדלקמן. אבל רבה ב"ב חנה דבכולי הש"ס היה בימי ר' יוחנן, ובן בנו של חנה — להכי קאמר בר בר. וי"מ דשם אביו בר חנה, ולא יתכן, כדאמר בהמוכר את הספינה (ב"ב דף עד.): "כל בר חנה סיכסא":
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:7:1.english: Rabba bar Ḥana - We read [in our text]: For if [the reading were] Rabba bar bar Ḥana, if so, he would be the grandson of Ḥana, whereas here it implies that he was the son of Rabbi Ḥiyya's brother [i.e., his nephew], and Ḥana was the brother of Rabbi Ḥiyya, as [stated] below. However, the Rabba bar bar Ḥana [who is mentioned] throughout the Talmud lived in the days of Rabbi Yochanan and was the grandson of Ḥana; that is why it says "bar bar" [son of the son of]. And some explain that his father's name was Bar Ḥana, but [this] is not plausible, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] Hamokher Et Hasefinah (Bava Batra 74a): "Every Bar Ḥana is a fool!"

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:8:1.hebrew: נקיטנא רשות מאבא מרי ואבא מרי מרב - פי': ואבא מרי נטל רשות מרב, דמי שיש לו רשות יכול ליתן רשות, כענין שמצינו (לקמן סנהדרין דף יג:) לענין דיני קנסות, דמי שהוא סמוך יכול לסמוך, ויהיב ליה רשותא למידן דיני קנסות, כדאמרינן (שם): "ברם זכור אותו האיש לטוב, שאלמלא הוא בטלו דיני קנסות". ואע"פ שהוצרך רבי חייא ליטול רשות מרבי בשביל רבה בר חנה ורב — שמא בעירו של רבי היה, ובעירו לא היה רשאי אדם ליתן רשות אלא רבי. אבל אין סברא לומר דרבה בר הונא היה בימי רבי:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 5a:8:1.english: "I received permission from my father, my master, and my father, my master from Rav" - Explanation: And my father, my master received permission from Rav — for one who has permission can grant permission, similar to that which we find (below, Sanhedrin 13b) with regard to cases of fines, that one who is ordained can ordain [others] and grant them permission to judge cases of fines, as we say (there): "Indeed, remember that man for good, for were it not for him, cases of fines would have ceased." And even though Rabbi Ḥiyya needed to obtain permission from Rabbi on behalf of Rabba bar Ḥana and Rav — perhaps it was in Rabbi's town, and in his town no person was permitted to grant permission other than Rabbi. But it is not reasonable to say that Rabba bar Huna was [alive] in the days of Rabbi.
